backlog.spec: In train(), compile the forward step with mode="reduce-overhead" instead of mode="max-autotune" (or keep max-autotune for the model and add reduce-overhead to forward_step only) so that per-step kernel launch overhead is replaced by CUDA graph replay. Keep fullgraph=True. Because the batch size is fixed at 1536 and drop_last=True, all training batches have identical shape, so graph capture is valid. Compilation is untimed, so only the per-step runtime changes. Check that the optimizer step outside the compiled region is not affected.
backlog.title: CUDA-graph training step

backlog.spec: In CifarLoader.__iter__, instead of indexing images[idxs] and labels[idxs] for every batch (a gather copy per step), apply the random permutation once per epoch to the full augmented image and label tensors (images = images[perm], labels_perm = labels[perm]) and then take contiguous slices of batch_size. This keeps the same sampling distribution (a fresh random permutation each epoch with drop_last) and removes the per-batch gather kernels. Keep augmentation applied before the permutation as it is now.
backlog.title: Pre-shuffled epoch tensor

backlog.spec: Replace the alternating-epoch whole-dataset flip with an independent random flip per sample in every epoch. In the loader, the pre-flipped copy is no longer needed; apply batch_flip_lr to the normalised images at the start of each epoch (it is already compiled). Keep the random 2-pixel translation and color jitter unchanged. This trades the current flip diversity scheme for per-sample flips and may change the optimum epoch count slightly, so leave EPOCHS unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-sample random horizontal flip

backlog.spec: Add a random erasing (cutout) step to the per-epoch augmentation: for each image, with probability 0.5, zero out a random 8x8 square (location uniform over valid positions, applied with a vectorised mask built from arange comparisons, compiled like the other augment helpers). Apply after translation and before color jitter, so the zeroed region is in normalised space. Only add this if it does not add a visible per-epoch cost.
backlog.title: Cutout regularisation

backlog.spec: Increase TRANSLATE from 2 to 3 so that the random crop offset ranges over 7 positions per axis instead of 5, with the reflect padding automatically sized by the existing pad logic. Also change the test-time pad in infer's _get_tta_logits from 1 to match a 2-pixel shift set only if accuracy holds. This is a one-constant change to the augmentation strength; it mainly tests whether the small 60-epoch-equivalent budget is under- or over-regularised by translation.
backlog.title: Larger translation with reflect pad

backlog.spec: Replace the linear-to-zero decay for the Muon learning rate (lr_factor2 = 1 - step/total) with a cosine decay, lr_factor2 = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*step/total)). Keep the bias and head SGD schedules linear. Also keep the Muon target magnitude schedule inside _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 as it is. The cosine shape keeps more learning rate in the middle of training and drops it faster at the end.
backlog.title: Cosine decay for Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Add a short linear warm-up to the Muon learning rate: over the first 3% of total_train_steps, multiply the Muon lr factor by step/warm_steps, then apply the existing linear decay for the rest. Implement inside the per-step lr computation in train() (lr_factor2 = min(1, step/warm_steps) * (1 - step*lr_factor2_base)). This protects the first Newton-Schulz-orthogonalised updates, which are the largest relative steps early on.
backlog.title: Warm-up for Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 to MUON_MOMENTUM (0.655) at about 10% of total steps, in the optimizer's step (update group['momentum'] each step, which Muon reads from the param group). Momentum for the early steps is then higher for smoother directions, and the final value matches the tuned constant. Keep the Nesterov form unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warm-up

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, increase the number of Newton-Schulz iterations from 3 to 5 by repeating the A/B/X update block two more times. Accuracy of the orthogonalisation improves, at the cost of extra batched matmuls on tiny (≤256x256 padded) matrices. Because the step is compiled, check it adds little wall time; if the gain is negligible the variant is not worth keeping.
backlog.title: Five Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation from 3 to 2 iterations in _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 and compensate by using the existing target magnitude schedule as is. The per-step matmul count drops by about a third for the Muon part. This is an explicit speed/accuracy trade; the expected effect is a small accuracy loss but a shorter per-step time, which may be net-positive in cost.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the convolution and head weights during training (decay about 0.99 per step, updated after each optimizer step with torch._foreach_lerp_ or foreach mul/add), and copy the EMA weights into the model at the end of train(). BatchNorm running stats are left as is. The averaged weights often generalise better than the final iterate when the learning rate decays to zero, so this should be checked for accuracy gain; its cost is one extra foreach update per step.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for prediction

backlog.spec: Set nesterov=False for the Muon optimizer in train() (it is currently True) so that the orthogonalised update uses the plain momentum buffer. This is a single-flag change to test whether the Nesterov look-ahead is useful at this learning rate. It removes one foreach add per step.
backlog.title: Nesterov off for Muon

backlog.spec: Set the Muon weight decay to zero (pass weight_decay=0.0 instead of wd to the Muon constructor) and keep weight decay only on the SGD bias and head groups. Muon updates are already norm-controlled by the orthogonalisation, so decay may be redundant for the convolution filters. This removes one foreach mul per step and tests whether the tuned decay value is hurting accuracy.
backlog.title: Remove weight decay from Muon

backlog.spec: Make LABEL_SMOOTHING time-dependent: start at 0.0 at the first step and rise linearly to 0.09 by the middle of training, then hold. The loss is computed inside forward_step, so pass the current smoothing value as a tensor argument to the compiled function to avoid recompilation (or pre-compute a small table). Early training then fits hard targets, while later epochs get the regularisation.
backlog.title: Label smoothing ramp

backlog.spec: Not implemented as mixup. Instead, in forward_step, average the loss over both the image and its horizontally flipped version (two forward passes of the same batch concatenated along the batch dimension, one cross_entropy over the concatenated logits and labels). This doubles the effective per-step compute, so reduce EPOCHS proportionally to keep the time budget. The aim is to make the flip symmetry explicit in the loss rather than only in the data.
backlog.title: Mixup-free soft target from flip ensemble

backlog.spec: Start training with a smaller batch (for example 512) and increase it linearly to BATCH_SIZE (1536) over the first 30% of steps, by changing the loader's batch size between epochs and recomputing the number of steps per epoch. Keep total_train_steps tied to the sample budget. Because torch.compile sees new shapes, the compiled forward step may recompile at each batch size, so restrict to two or three discrete sizes and mark dynamic=False. Smaller early batches give more updates when the network is far from converged.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp

backlog.spec: Increase BATCH_SIZE from 1536 to 2048 and scale the learning rates so that the per-sample step size is kept: multiply BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(2048/1536) approximately 1.155. Keep the epoch count fixed. Larger batches give higher GPU utilisation on the A4000 and fewer optimizer steps, which may reduce wall time; the learning-rate rescale is the only accuracy-sensitive part.
backlog.title: Larger batch size

backlog.spec: Decrease BATCH_SIZE from 1536 to 1024 and scale BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(1024/1536) approximately 0.816 to keep the per-sample step size comparable. Keep epochs fixed. This doubles the number of optimizer steps, so Muon orthogonalisation and norm recomputation cost more; the run tests whether more updates beat per-step cost on this GPU.
backlog.title: Smaller batch size

backlog.spec: Add an identity shortcut around conv2 within ConvGroup for blocks where channels_in equals channels_out (block2 and block3 do not match block1's 64 to 256 input, so only use it for block3's 256 to 256 path). Implement as x = x + conv2_output before norm2 (or after norm2, keeping the BatchNorm without scale). The shortcut lets gradients flow through the deeper block at negligible extra compute.
backlog.title: Residual connection in ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Replace the nn.MaxPool2d(2) in each ConvGroup with a 2x2 average pool, leaving the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) unchanged. Max pooling is the usual choice in this speedrun family, but average pooling after a linear-ish conv may give smoother gradients. This is a single-layer swap with identical output shape and near-zero compute change.
backlog.title: Average pooling instead of max pooling

backlog.spec: Reduce the block3 width from 256 to 192 (widths dict block3=192) and adjust the head input accordingly, which the code already derives from widths['block3']. This cuts the matmul cost of the last ConvGroup by about 44 percent in the convolution FLOPs, reducing per-step time. Accuracy will drop slightly, so compare against the time saved; the epoch count is unchanged.
backlog.title: Narrower final block

backlog.spec: Increase block1 width from 64 to 96 (widths dict block1=96). Block 1 operates at the highest resolution after the whitening layer and the first pooling, so extra width there adds capacity mostly at a modest compute cost. Because block2 takes block1's output as input, the ConvGroup constructor already adapts. Check that the whitening output width (24 channels) is still consistent with the first ConvGroup.
backlog.title: Wider first block

backlog.spec: Remove the leading nn.GELU() applied to the whitening output in self.layers (the whitening layer has a bias, and the first ConvGroup's conv1 is linear anyway). This drops one elementwise kernel per forward and backward pass. Verify the whitened features keep their sign information; if accuracy drops, revert.
backlog.title: Replace GELU at input with identity

backlog.spec: Add a single learnable scalar multiplier on the head logits, initialised to 1.0 and trained with the head's SGD group (no weight decay), in addition to the existing 1/x.size(-1) scale. The network can then adjust the logit sharpness, which interacts with label smoothing. This adds one parameter and essentially no compute.
backlog.title: Learned scalar temperature on the head

backlog.spec: Increase WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 1.0 so the whitening-layer bias keeps training for the first full epoch. Currently the bias only trains for a short initial window and then freezes via whiten_bias_grad. Keep BIAS_LR and the linear decay for that group as they are. This is a one-constant change to test whether the learned input offset helps.
backlog.title: Longer whitening-bias training

backlog.spec: In train(), compute the whitening initialisation from more training images (for example 5000 instead of 960) by changing the slice train_loader.normalize(train_loader.images[:960]) to a larger slice, and keep eps at 0.0005. The patch covariance is then estimated from more data, which can give a better-conditioned whitening filter. The computation is in train() and only uses the current run's images, so it is allowed; it costs a little extra time in the covariance step, so check the net effect.
backlog.title: Whitening init from more images

backlog.spec: In infer's tta path, extend the views for the uncertain subset from two shifted crops plus the original to four shifted corner crops (pad=1, adding the crop_tr and crop_bl windows from the reflect-padded input), with flips, so the average is over 8 views. The change is inside _get_tta_logits and only affects the 25 percent least-confident images. It may recover a little accuracy at a small prediction-time cost.
backlog.title: Four-view test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: Increase UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE in the tta function from 0.25 to 0.5, so that the shift and flip ensemble is applied to half the test set rather than a quarter. This is a constant change in the prediction function and does not alter the model. It trades a little extra prediction time for a possible accuracy gain on less confident images.
backlog.title: Larger uncertain fraction for TTA

backlog.spec: Remove the confidence-based selection in predict and apply the full flip and shift ensemble (the _get_tta_logits path) to every test image, dropping the topk step. This simplifies the prediction function and makes its cost deterministic. Compare accuracy and prediction time against the current 25 percent selection; the expected gain is small but the code becomes simpler.
backlog.title: Confidence-free TTA on all images

backlog.spec: Maintain a running average of the model weights over the final 20 percent of training steps (average sampled every few steps, only convolution and head weights), and load the average into the model before predict. Because the learning rate is near zero at the end, the averaged weights may match or beat the last iterate. Implement the averaging with foreach ops so the overhead is small. This complements the EMA idea but uses a uniform window.
backlog.title: Stochastic weight averaging over last epochs

backlog.spec: Move the 10x256 linear head weight out of the Nesterov SGD group and into the Muon optimizer, so it gets the same orthogonalised, norm-scaled update as the conv filters. Keep its own learning rate at HEAD_LR, keep the linear-to-zero decay, and keep the 1/x.size(-1) logit scaling in forward. Only the optimizer grouping changes; the Muon step itself is untouched.
backlog.title: Orthogonalised head via Muon

backlog.spec: Remove the frozen weight in the BatchNorm subclass (set weight.requires_grad = True instead of False) so each BN layer learns a per-channel scale alongside its bias. Initialise the scale to one as PyTorch does, and check that the norm parameters are already in the bias group so they are trained by SGD with the existing bias learning rate and weight decay. Nothing else in the script changes.
backlog.title: Learnable BatchNorm scale

backlog.spec: During the first ~40% of training steps, downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 with bilinear interpolation (antialias on), and switch to the native 32x32 for the rest. The whitening conv and max-pool stack are size-agnostic, so the head still sees a 1x1 map after the final MaxPool2d(3) only at 32; to keep it consistent, use adaptive average pooling to 1x1 in the head path only if the spatial size is not 32. Compile both shapes once in the untimed warm-up if possible, or accept one recompile. This aims to cut time per early step substantially at similar final accuracy.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution from 24 to 32 pixels

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup for the blocks whose input and output widths match (block2 and block3), wrap the conv2 to norm2 branch with a stochastic-depth gate: during training, drop the whole branch per sample with probability 0.1 and rescale the kept branch by 1/(1-0.1); at eval, keep the branch unscaled. Add this as a residual sum with the block input, so the path is identity when the branch is dropped. Keep the rest of the network and schedules as they are. The aim is a regulariser for the short run without extra compute.
backlog.title: Stochastic depth on the second conv of blocks 2 and 3

backlog.spec: In the loader, keep the existing alternating-epoch flip for the first 80 percent of total_train_steps, then stop flipping entirely for the last 20 percent so the final fits see only the native orientation that the test set uses. Implement this by checking the global step against 0.8*total_train_steps inside train(), and passing a flag that suppresses the epoch-parity flip in __iter__. Brightness, contrast and translation stay on throughout.
backlog.title: Switch off horizontal flip for the final 20 percent of steps

backlog.spec: Add a per-sample random scale augmentation to the training batch: for each image draw a zoom factor uniformly in [0.9, 1.1], resample the 32x32 image with an affine grid (torch.nn.functional.affine_grid and grid_sample, bilinear, border padding) on top of the existing 2-pixel translation, and keep the flip and colour jitter as they are. Use one batched grid_sample call inside a compiled helper, drawing the randomness on the GPU. This adds a geometric augmentation axis that the current translation-only pipeline lacks.
backlog.title: Random zoom jitter of plus or minus 10 percent

backlog.spec: At roughly 50 percent of total_train_steps, copy the current model weights into a frozen teacher (run it under no_grad in eval mode, with half precision). For the remaining steps, replace the one-hot target by a mix of 0.5 times the smoothed label and 0.5 times the teacher softmax on the same augmented batch, with the cross-entropy computed against this soft target. Nothing from the teacher is carried across runs; it is created inside train() from the current run's own data. The aim is a cheap knowledge-distillation regulariser that may improve the final accuracy at a modest time cost.
backlog.title: Self-distillation from a mid-run snapshot

backlog.spec: After the final MaxPool2d(3) and the flatten in CifarNet.forward, apply dropout with probability 0.1 to the 256-dimensional feature vector during training only (use the module's training flag so predict is unchanged). Place the dropout as a new nn.Dropout module created in __init__ so torch.compile sees it cleanly. Keep the head, its learning rate and the 1/x.size(-1) scaling unchanged. This is a small, cheap regulariser on the only layer that feeds the classifier.
backlog.title: Dropout on pooled features before the head

backlog.spec: Replace the nn.SiLU activation in ConvGroup (both uses) with a squared ReLU, defined as relu(x) squared, implemented as a small nn.Module whose forward returns F.relu(x).square(). Leave the input GELU and every other part of the network unchanged. Because squared ReLU has a different scale than SiLU, the following batch norm (which has no learned scale unless changed) absorbs the scale; keep the rest of the schedule as is. Expect a different time and accuracy trade-off, so check both.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU in place of SiLU

backlog.spec: Within the compiled forward_step, compute per-sample cross-entropy with label smoothing (reduction none), then multiply each sample's loss by a weight w = (1 - p_true)^gamma with gamma = 0.5, detached from the graph, normalised so that the batch mean weight is one. Sum the weighted losses as the training loss so the total gradient scale matches the current sum reduction. This is a focal-style reweighting that puts more gradient on hard examples in a short run without changing the data pipeline.
backlog.title: Confidence-weighted loss on each batch

backlog.spec: In BatchNorm (or a wrapper used in ConvGroup), compute the normalisation statistics over sub-batches of 256 samples instead of the full 1536-sample batch. In forward, reshape (N, C, H, W) to (N/256, 256, C, H, W) or fold the sub-batch index into the batch dimension, take mean and variance per sub-batch, normalise, then reshape back. Keep running statistics as the average over sub-batches so predict uses them unchanged. This adds per-sub-batch noise that acts as a regulariser and may improve generalisation at no extra time cost. Keep BATCH_SIZE, the optimiser and the schedule unchanged.
backlog.title: Ghost batch norm with 256-sample sub-batches

backlog.spec: In the training loop, for each batch with probability 0.3 while step < 0.5 * total_train_steps, sample lambda from Beta(1,1) (or uniform), pick a random permutation of the batch, and paste a rectangular patch of the permuted images into the current images. The rectangle has side lengths proportional to sqrt(1 - lambda) of the 24 or 32 pixel side and a random centre. Set the labels to a mix of the two one-hot vectors weighted by the patch area ratio, and compute the loss as the weighted sum of the two cross-entropies with the existing label smoothing. Turn CutMix off for the second half so the final steps fit the data cleanly.
backlog.title: CutMix on a fraction of batches during the first half of training

backlog.spec: In Muon.step, multiply the learning rate applied to each filter's orthogonalised update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) where rows and cols are the reshaped dimensions (reshaped_D and reshaped_K in the existing meta data). This is the usual shape-aware scaling that keeps update magnitude consistent across layers of different width. The block1, block2 and block3 convolutions have different aspect ratios, so this changes their effective learning rates differently. Keep the base MUON_LR, the Newton-Schulz coefficients and the linear decay unchanged, and do not touch the norm-scaling logic.
backlog.title: Per-layer Muon learning-rate scaling by fan-out over fan-in

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, change the order to conv1, norm1, activation, conv2, pool, norm2, activation. Pooling after conv2 means conv2 runs at the full spatial resolution, which is more expensive, so this is not a clear speed win by itself. Instead, consider the reverse arrangement, where conv1 runs at full resolution and conv2 runs after the pool at half resolution, and check the step time. Keep the widths, BatchNorm placement and activation unchanged. The aim is a different accuracy-per-FLOP trade-off in each block; time the run and keep the change only if the cost improves.
backlog.title: Move the first max-pool after the second convolution in each block

backlog.spec: Replace nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in CifarNet.layers with a module that returns the concatenation of the spatial max and the spatial mean along the channel axis, giving 512 features for block3 width 256. Change the head to nn.Linear(512, 10, bias=False) and keep the division by x.size(-1) in forward, using the new feature count in place of the old one so the output scale is comparable. Mean pooling gives the head a smoother global signal alongside the peak response. Keep everything else unchanged, including the head LR and weight decay.
backlog.title: Concatenated max and mean pooling before the head

backlog.spec: Keep the learning rate at its initial value for the first 35 percent of total_train_steps, then decay it linearly to zero over the remaining 65 percent. Apply the same multiplier to the Muon group, the SGD bias group and the head group, so the lr_factor1 whiten-bias schedule stays as it is. Implement this by replacing lr_factor2 = 1 - step * lr_factor2_base with a function that returns 1 while step is below 0.35 * total_train_steps and then falls linearly to 0 at total_train_steps. Keep the Muon target-magnitude schedule as is.
backlog.title: Flat-then-decay learning-rate schedule for both optimisers

backlog.spec: In train(), disable the brightness and contrast jitter once step reaches 0.8 * total_train_steps, so the last fifth of training sees clean normalised images. Implement this by making CifarLoader.__iter__ take the current step or a flag, or by setting the color_jitter enabled flag on the loader when the threshold is crossed; the loader's epoch-level augmentation is applied once per epoch, so apply the switch at the start of the epoch that contains the threshold. Keep flip and translation unchanged. This is a data-side annealing that removes a source of train-test mismatch near the end of training.
backlog.title: Stop colour jitter for the final 20 percent of steps

backlog.spec: In predict(), make a deep copy of the model, put the copy in train mode with BatchNorm momentum set to None (cumulative average), reset its running statistics, and run one forward pass over the test images in batches of 2000 under torch.no_grad() to recompute the running mean and variance. Then switch the copy to eval mode and run the existing infer(tta_level=2) path on it. The original model is never modified, so the predict-must-not-change-the-model rule holds. This adapts normalisation to the test distribution and may help when test statistics differ slightly from the augmented training batches. Note that the copy costs time, so check the run time.
backlog.title: Test-time BatchNorm recalibration on the test set

backlog.spec: In predict(), bilinearly upsample the normalised test images from 32 to 36 or 40 pixels (antialias off) before calling the model, leaving the TTA views to be built from the original size or from the upsampled size consistently. The network has max pooling and an adaptive max pool, so it accepts any input size. Training used 24 pixels for the first 40 percent of steps and 32 afterwards, so a slightly larger test resolution can match the apparent object scale that the adaptive pool sees, as in the FixRes effect. Try 36 first. Keep the training loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Upsample test images before inference (FixRes-style test resolution)

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 24-pixel low-resolution phase with per-batch random resolution during the first 60 percent of steps. For each batch, draw a size uniformly from {24, 26, 28, 30, 32} and bilinearly resize the batch to that size, with antialias on when downsampling. Use the full 32 pixels for the remaining steps. Each batch then sees a different scale, which may act as scale augmentation and reduce the mismatch between the low-resolution phase and the full-resolution phase. Keep the translation and flip augmentation unchanged. Because the forward step is compiled with fullgraph, mark the possible sizes as separate compiled graphs or use dynamic=False and accept a few recompilations, which are not timed.
backlog.title: Per-batch random resolution jitter between 24 and 32 pixels

backlog.spec: Replace the single 24-pixel stage with a staged ramp. Define resolutions 20, 24, 28, 32 and switch to the next one at 25%, 50% and 75% of total_train_steps, so the first quarter runs at 20x20 and the last quarter at 32x32. Keep the bilinear antialiased F.interpolate call, and compute the target size from the step counter in train(). Leave the schedules, EPOCHS and the whitening init unchanged. The goal is to cut time with the same accuracy and to test whether a smooth ramp beats the fixed 24-then-32 switch.
backlog.title: Smooth multi-stage progressive resolution

backlog.spec: After the first 2 epochs, at the start of each epoch keep only the 75% of training samples with the highest loss recorded in the previous epoch, and drop the rest for that epoch. Record per-sample loss from the forward pass (reduction='none' in a separate uncompiled loss computation on the batch, or store it from the compiled forward). Reduce total_train_steps by the same pruning fraction so that the LR schedules still reach zero at the end, which gives fewer steps and less time. Keep the shuffling and the drop_last logic inside the loader.
backlog.title: Hard-example pruning with a shortened step budget

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, replace the sequence conv1 (stride 1) then MaxPool2d(2) with a single 3x3 convolution with stride 2 and padding 1, keeping the same in and out channels. This halves the spatial size before conv2 and cuts the compute of the conv2 layers in every block. Keep norm1, the SiLU and the rest of the network the same. Make the Conv class accept a stride argument, and keep the dirac init on the reset path, adjusted for the stride.
backlog.title: Strided convolution replaces conv1 plus max-pool

backlog.spec: Replace the linear head with a cosine classifier. L2-normalise the 256-dim pooled features and the head weight rows, take their dot product, and multiply by a fixed scale s=10 in place of the current head(x)/x.size(-1) division. Keep head_lr and weight decay for the head weight. This removes the scale dependence of the logits, which is a bold change to the output geometry, and it may interact with label smoothing and the head LR. Update reset() so the head weight init still uses a sensible std.
backlog.title: Scaled cosine-similarity classifier head

backlog.spec: Once step reaches 60% of total_train_steps, stop updating the parameters of ConvGroup 1 (conv1, conv2, norm1, norm2). Set requires_grad to False on those tensors and remove them from the Muon and SGD parameter lists, or zero their LR. Do this once at the boundary, then let torch.compile recompile for the new graph. The backward pass through block1 is then skipped for the remaining 40% of steps, which saves time. The idea is that the early features are settled by then and the later blocks can adapt.
backlog.title: Freeze the first block after 60 percent of training

backlog.spec: Insert nn.Dropout2d with p=0.1 right after the whitening convolution and the GELU, before ConvGroup 1. Apply it only in train mode, so predict is unchanged. Whitened channels are highly correlated, so channel-wise dropout forces redundancy across the filters that the orthogonalised Muon updates shape. Keep the rest of the network and the optimizer as they are. Dropout is inactive in eval, so the TTA path is unaffected.
backlog.title: Dropout on the whitened input channels

backlog.spec: In forward_step, replace the cross-entropy with a focal-modulated version. Compute per-sample log-probabilities with label smoothing, take p_t as the exponentiated log-prob of the true class, and weight each sample's loss by (1 - p_t)^gamma with gamma=0.5. Sum over the batch as the current code does, so the loss scale and the LR stay comparable. Use detach on the weight so that the gradient only flows through the log-prob term. This puts more weight on hard, low-confidence samples without any extra forward pass.
backlog.title: Focal modulation on the cross-entropy loss

backlog.spec: Each sampled batch contains every image twice, each copy with an independent random translation, flip decision and colour jitter, so the effective batch is 2x BATCH_SIZE with the same number of forward passes per image. Halve the number of optimizer steps (total_train_steps and whiten_bias_train_steps are computed from the reduced count) so that wall time is roughly the same as now. Keep the learning-rate schedules tied to the new step count. This tests whether doubling augmentation diversity per update helps a short run.
backlog.title: Repeated augmentation with halved step budget

backlog.spec: In infer's _get_tta_logits, replace the mean over views of raw logits with a mean of softmax probabilities, then take the log to return logits again. Keep the same 3 base views and flips, and keep the mixing with the initial logits for the uncertain 25 percent. The change keeps the cost identical, and only the way views are combined is different. Make sure the returned tensor is still a log-probability that the harness can take as logits.
backlog.title: Probability averaging in the test-time ensemble

backlog.spec: In predict's tta path, pick the images that get extra test-time views by the top-2 logit margin instead of the top-1 softmax confidence. Compute margin = top1 logit minus top2 logit from the initial logits, and take the 25 percent with the smallest margin using torch.topk with largest=False. Keep the rest of the TTA the same, including the 3 base views and flips. This is a cheap change to the selection rule that may pick the images that are actually close to a decision boundary.
backlog.title: Margin-based selection of uncertain test images

cand.description: Drops the confidence-based top-25% selection in predict's tta function so the flip and shift ensemble (_get_tta_logits) runs on every test image in fixed 2000-image batches, removing the initial pass and topk.

incumbent.description: Trains the first 40% of steps on batches bilinearly downsampled (antialiased) to 24x24, with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so the network works at both sizes, to cut early-step time at similar accuracy.

memo:
Only slot 6 helped: training the first 40% of steps on 24x24 downsampled batches scored -0.1535 and -0.1443 over 2 runs (incumbent -0.1427). It carries a tripwire flag, so check that before trusting it. Progressive resolution, which cuts time at similar accuracy, is the promising direction. Next: vary the low-res fraction and resolution (e.g. 50% of steps, 20x20), or try a smooth ramp. Replicate near-incumbent candidates.

Did not help: cosine Muon decay (0.0839), 3% warm-up (0.0735), 3 px translation (0.0568), extra TTA views (0.0101), per-sample flip (-0.0733, worse than the incumbent), removing the leading GELU (0.1867), the conv2 shortcut (-0.0011), label smoothing ramp (-0.1480), max+avg pooling (-0.0343), stopping flip late (-0.1175), jitter off late (-0.1347), non-Nesterov Muon (0.0010). Newton-Schulz at 5 iterations was a disaster (9.1982), so leave the Muon internals alone. Squared-ReLU crashed twice (slots 11 and 12). Schedule and augmentation tweaks look well tuned.
